title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Civil Engineering (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Civil Engineering (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Select the behavior of Stress-Strain curve for low concrete grade
options: Sharper the peak of the curve
The Behavior cannot be affected by the strength of the concrete
questions.explanation: Low concrete grades typically exhibit less failure strain.

questions.questionText: Which of the following design philosophy uses factor of safety for materials and loads?
questions.explanation: The Limit State Design Method applies partial safety factors to both materials (γm) and loads (γf) to account for uncertainties, unlike Working Stress Method which uses a single factor of safety.

questions.questionText: A RC beam with 250 mm width and 400mm effective depth is provided with 8 mm – 2 legged stirrups at 150 mm c/c spacing at a particular section. Calculate the shear resistance at that particular section. If the shear capacity of the concrete is 30.58kN and steel having f yd = 300MPa is used.
questions.explanation: The shear resistance = concrete contribution + steel contribution. Steel contribution = (Asv × fyd × d)/s = (2 × π × 4² × 300 × 400)/150 = 80.4kN. Total = 30.58 + 80.4 = 111kN.

questions.questionText: Which type of beam is selected when the depth of the beam is limited by the architect?
questions.explanation: Doubly reinforced beams are used when depth is limited.

questions.questionText: When moment redistribution at the interior supports of a slab is done the sum of distribution factors of all the members meeting at any joint is always
questions.explanation: In moment distribution method, the sum of distribution factors at any joint must equal 1 as it represents the proportional distribution of unbalanced moments among connecting members.

questions.questionText: As per EBCS which one of the following statements is not correct about the curtailment of positive reinforcement in a continuous member?
options: Minimum two bars should extend throughout.
At least one third bars should extend into the support for a ¾ rd development of length.
Cut-off bars shall extend for a distance not less than effective depth of the member beyond theoretical cut-off point.
Cut-off bars shall extend for a distance not less than 12 times the bar diameter beyond theoretical cut-off point.
questions.explanation: The statement regarding the extension of bars into the support is incorrect.

questions.questionText: The length between points of inflection of columns is
questions.explanation: The effective buckling length is the length between points of inflection.

questions.questionText: Second order effect is considered for
questions.explanation: Second order effects are significant in slender columns.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of applying flat slabs?
questions.explanation: Maximum depth is not an advantage of flat slabs.

questions.questionText: Plastic hinges will not be formed at a points of
questions.explanation: Plastic hinges do not form at points of maximum shear.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is applicable when the shape of slabs is irregular, there is presence of openings and having varied support conditions?
questions.explanation: The Yield Line Method is used for irregular slab shapes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the reason behind commonly using rolled steel I-sections as beams?
options: Large moment of inertia with less cross-sectional area
Large moment of resistance as compared to other section
questions.explanation: Low mass to volume ratio is not a reason for using rolled steel I-sections.

questions.questionText: For structural collapse and structural component failure during design of steel structures, which limit state category is applied?
questions.explanation: The ultimate limit state is applied for structural collapse.

questions.questionText: The most economical section for a column is
questions.explanation: Tubular sections are often the most economical for columns.

questions.questionText: Web crippling generally occurs at the point where
questions.explanation: Web crippling occurs where concentrated loads are applied.

questions.questionText: Select the true statement about beam-column members
options: They resist both Flexural and axial actions
questions.explanation: Beam-column members resist both flexural and axial actions.

questions.questionText: Strength of bolt is
options: Minimum of shear strength and bearing capacity of bolt
Maximum of shear strength and bearing capacity of bolt
questions.explanation: The strength of a bolt is determined by the minimum of its shear strength and bearing capacity.

questions.questionText: What design state must be considered to limit crack growth under repetitive loads to prevent fracture during the design life of the bridge?
questions.explanation: The Fatigue and Fracture limit state is crucial for preventing crack growth.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a requirement for bridge site selection?
options: Minimum disturbing influence of larger tributaries
questions.explanation: Permitting parallel crossing is not a requirement for bridge site selection.

questions.questionText: For which loads do you consider dynamic load allowance factor?
questions.explanation: Dynamic load allowance factors are considered for design truck loads.

questions.questionText: Which is true about loading on Bridge?
options: Wind load consideration in Small and low bridge
Add dynamic effect to Pedestrian load
Avoid dynamic effect to Design Truck load
Wind load consideration in Longer span bridge
questions.explanation: Wind load considerations are particularly important for longer span bridges.

questions.questionText: The governing action effect which is observed only in Box-Girder bridge is
questions.explanation: Torsion is a significant effect in box-girder bridges.

questions.questionText: What is the role of Bearing in bridge structure?
options: Accommodate relative movements between superstructure and substructure
It is a wall constructed on both sides of the abutment to support it
questions.explanation: Bearings accommodate movements between the superstructure and substructure.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the behavior of a beam cross section having larger plastic moment and elastic moment ratio?
questions.explanation: A beam with a larger plastic moment to elastic moment ratio typically exhibits high ductility.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not true about a strong band?
options: It is an internal beam usually having the same depth as the remainder of the slab
It is a strip at unsupported edge
It acts as a support at the edge of opening
questions.explanation: A strong band typically contains a higher concentration of reinforcement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors does not influence earthquake resistance design?
questions.explanation: Wind location does not directly influence earthquake resistance design.

questions.questionText: Structures should be designed such that:
options: Minor and frequent earthquakes can collapse the structure
Moderate earthquakes can cause damage to the structure
Major earthquakes should not cause any damage to the structure and the structure should be functional
Minor earthquake should not cause any damage to the structure and the structure should be functional
questions.explanation: Structures should be designed to withstand minor earthquakes without damage.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct wind load transferring system of a building?
questions.explanation: The correct sequence for wind load transfer is Roof - Purlins - Truss - Girder.

questions.questionText: Which of the following load combination is not possible?
options: Dead load + imposed load + wind load
Dead load + imposed load + earthquake load
Dead load + wind load + earthquake load
questions.explanation: The combination of dead load + wind load + earthquake load is typically not used.

questions.questionText: The following criteria should not be considered when selecting the Highway alignment and locating the route.
options: The alignment between two terminal control points should be short
Obstructions such as cemeteries, places of worship, and archaeological and historical monuments should be steered through.
The location should pass through agricultural land and national parks.
questions.explanation: Steering through obstructions is not a desirable criterion for highway alignment.

questions.questionText: Road is designed for a speed of 80 km/h on a horizontal curve with a superelevation of 8%. If the coefficient of side friction is 0.1, determine the minimum radius of the curve in meters required for safe vehicular movement.
questions.explanation: Using the formula R = V²/[127(e+f)] where V=80km/h, e=0.08, f=0.1, the radius R = 80²/[127(0.08+0.1)] = 279.5m, rounded to 280m.

questions.questionText: An existing road has a 200m long vertical curve, which connects an initial grade of +2.0% & a final grade of -3.0% intersecting at PVI station 2+100 an elevation of 2500. With these given parameters, which of the following is NOT true about the point of vertical curvature (PVC) and point of vertical tangency (PVT)?
questions.explanation: The elevation of PVT would be 2500 + (-3.0% × 100m) = 2500 - 3 = 2497m, not 2502m. Option D is incorrect.

questions.questionText: An existing road has a 200m long vertical curve which connects an initial grade of -2.0% & a final grade of +3.0% intersecting at PVI station 2+100 and elevation of 2500. With these given parameters, which of the following is NOT true about the point of vertical curvature (PVC) and point of vertical tangency (PVT)?
questions.explanation: The elevation of PVC should be 2500 + (-2.0% × -100m) = 2500 + 2 = 2502m, not 2498m. Option B is incorrect.

questions.questionText: The overhaul volume of 7200m3 is to be overhauled at an average overhaul distance of 2400m with a contract rate of 10 birr/(m3 - km). What is the overhauling cost of the earthwork?
questions.explanation: Overhauling cost = 7200m³ × 2.4km × 10 birr/(m³·km) = 172,800 birr.

questions.questionText: Which is NOT the possible solution to improve safety at a given intersection?
questions.explanation: Increasing the area of conflict does not improve safety.

questions.questionText: ______________ is defined as the excessive accumulated vertical deformation of pavement along the wheel path due to repeated traffic loading.
questions.explanation: Rutting is the term used for excessive vertical deformation in pavement.

questions.questionText: A plate-loading test using a plate of 305mm diameter was performed on the surface of the subgrade. A total load of 40kN was applied & a deflection of 2.54mm was measured. Assuming that the subgrade has a Poisson's ratio of 0.5, determine the elastic modulus of the subgrade. Use surface deflection, ωo = π (1 - v^2) 2E qa.
questions.explanation: The elastic modulus can be calculated using the given formula and parameters.

questions.questionText: Which percentage of Aggregate Impact Test (AIT) is more suitable for surface-course construction if you're a material engineer on a road project?
questions.explanation: A lower percentage is typically preferred for surface-course construction.

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the aggregate gradation of different aggregates. Label letters b, c, and d, respectively.
options: Uniformly graded, Gap graded, and Open-graded
Uniformly graded, Gap graded, and well graded
questions.explanation: The correct labeling of aggregate gradation types is provided.

questions.questionText: Which construction sequences can be argued to be the convenient procedure from the upward sub-base layer?
options: Prime coat, granular base, dense bituminous macadam, tack coat, and dense asphalt concrete
Granular base, prime coat, dense bituminous macadam, tack coat, and dense asphalt concrete
Tack coat, granular base, prime coat, dense bituminous macadam, and dense asphalt concrete
Granular base, tack coat, dense bituminous macadam, prime coat, and dense asphalt concrete
questions.explanation: The correct sequence for construction from the upward sub-base layer is provided.

questions.questionText: Traffic analysis indicated the estimated total cumulative repetition over the design period on the design lane and the corresponding mean equivalency factors or truck factor values for each vehicle class, as shown in the Table below. Vehicle class, i Cumulative repetition over the design period on the design lane Mean equivalency or truck factor per vehicle class Small Car 1,800,000 0.00 Bus 300,000 0.40 Medium Truck 1000,000 5.88 Heavy Truck 200,000 15.00 Truck-trailers 500,000 12.00 What should be the number of cumulative equivalent standard axles (ESAs) that need to be considered in the structural design of this highway?
During the cost-benefit analysis of Transport projects, financial analysis involves …….
options: Analyzing projects from the perspective of social benefit as a whole.
Assessing disturbance to the wildlife and population displacement.
Measuring all the effects of the project on the cash flow
Analysis of ecological effects of projects on the topography
questions.explanation: Financial analysis focuses on measuring the effects on cash flow.

questions.questionText: Six vehicles pass a 300-m highway segment in periods of 10, 12, 10, 15, 12, and 15 seconds, respectively. The time mean speed, ut is_____________.
questions.explanation: Time mean speed = n/Σ(1/vi) = 6/Σ(300/3600vi) where vi are speeds in m/s. Converting to speeds (m/s): 30, 25, 30, 20, 25, 20. Converting to km/h and averaging gives 87.57 km/h.

questions.questionText: If the model that describes the relationship between space mean speed, us (in km/hr), and density, k (in veh/km) on a highway segment is given as us = 120 -3*k (Which of the following is NOT true about the model?
options: Density at maximum flow is 20 veh/km
questions.explanation: Maximum flow occurs at k=20 veh/km, giving us=120-3×20=60 km/hr. Maximum flow = us×k = 60×20 = 1200 veh/hr, not 360 veh/hr. Option D is incorrect.

questions.questionText: The following values of PTSF and ATS have been determined based on the analysis of Two roadway segments. Segment PTSF (%) ATS (mi/h) 1 35 51 2 50 56 Determine the LOS if the roadway segments are Class I by using Table 1.
questions.explanation: The level of service can be determined based on the provided PTSF and ATS values.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a category of Traffic markings?
questions.explanation: Vertical markings are not typically categorized as traffic markings.

questions.questionText: If the traffic volume on a highway in 2020 is 7981 vehicles per day, with a predicted annual growth rate of 5%. What will be the traffic volume (vehicles per day) in the year 2030?
questions.explanation: Using the formula Vn = Vo(1+r)^n, where Vo=7981, r=0.05, n=10 years, Vn = 7981×(1.05)^10 = 7981×1.629 = 13,001, rounded to 13,000.

questions.questionText: Which of the following test is used to measure the workability of concrete?
options: Specific gravity and water absorption test
questions.explanation: The compacting factor test is used to measure the workability of concrete.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the material that has the highest strength weight ratio?
questions.explanation: Steel has the highest strength-to-weight ratio among common construction materials.

questions.questionText: From the standpoint of the economy in cement for a given water cement ratio, which aggregate shape is preferable to use in concrete?
questions.explanation: Rounded aggregates are preferred for economy in cement usage.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following cement types is used for the construction of Sewage and Water treatment plants?
questions.explanation: Sulphate resisting cement is used in environments with high sulphate exposure.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a technique used to prevent segregation in the concrete making process?
questions.explanation: Proper vibration/compaction to expel entrapped air helps prevent segregation by ensuring uniform distribution of aggregate particles throughout the concrete mix.

questions.questionText: Given the following information Aggregates Weights in different Conditions (gm) W agg W OD W SSD W SSD (in water) 1000 980.4 1009.8 652 The bulk specific gravity (SSD) of the aggregate is:
questions.explanation: The bulk specific gravity can be calculated using the provided weights.

questions.questionText: A local swelling of a finished plastered wall.
questions.explanation: Blistering refers to the local swelling of plastered surfaces.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about building elements?
options: Combined footings are frequently used to support loads which are close to property line.
The primary function of the floor is to provide a level surface with sufficient strength to support the imposed loads of people and furniture.
The location of the door should be located at the center of the length of a wall.
Roofs are strong visual elements in a building and thus affect the aesthetic beauty of a building.
questions.explanation: The location of doors is not strictly required to be at the center of the wall.

questions.questionText: Choose the best formwork type to be reused in large numbers for good finish.
questions.explanation: Plywood is often chosen for its reusability and finish quality.

questions.questionText: After how many stairs is a landing provided in public residential places?
questions.explanation: Landings are typically provided after 12 stairs in public buildings.

questions.questionText: Which drawing type is used to show the design materials, dimensions, and final appearance of the exterior of a building?
questions.explanation: Elevation plans depict the exterior appearance and dimensions of a building.

questions.questionText: Choose the recommended foundation type, where a large spacing between two columns creates a situation where a continuous footing is uneconomical due to the usage of a large quantity of concrete.
questions.explanation: Strap footings are recommended for large spacing between columns.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT one of the functions of management based on Henry Fayol's classification?
questions.explanation: Actuating is not typically listed as a primary function in Fayol's management principles.

questions.questionText: Project X is expected to finish within 60 working days having a predetermined supervision at 30th day with a status of 50% completion. But the status of the project at 30th day is 40%. What will be the total project duration if the remaining work continues with the same progress?
questions.explanation: The total project duration can be estimated based on the current progress.

questions.questionText: If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earliest start and finish, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, and TF and FF are total float and free float, then the following relation is NOT true.
options: TF i = LS i – ES i
FF i = Max (ES i+1) - EF i
questions.explanation: The relation for free float is not correctly stated.

questions.questionText: In quality management system the correct cycle to improve quality is?
questions.explanation: The correct cycle for quality improvement is Plan - Do - Check - Act.

questions.questionText: Which step comes first in the risk management process of construction projects?
questions.explanation: Establishing the context is the first step in the risk management process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about safety risk?
options: Safety risks affect people by exposure to hazard
In safety risk the results of an accident are immediate
Safety risk is often a hidden danger
Safety risks are often difficult to assess
questions.explanation: Safety risks typically result in immediate consequences from accidents.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct statement.
options: The main difference between specification and drawing is that specification should generally show dimensions, extents, size, shape, and location of component parts.
Manufacturer's specifications are intended to be used as reference standard in the construction of a project.
All dimensions should be measured to the nearest 0.01m.
Centre line method is suitable only when the cross sections of all walls are unequal.
questions.explanation: All dimensions should be measured accurately, typically to the nearest 0.01m.

questions.questionText: In preparing cement concrete by volume the most commonly used size of the wooden box used to measure aggregate in Ethiopia is.
questions.explanation: The commonly used size for measuring aggregates in Ethiopia is 18 cm x 40 cm x 50 cm.

questions.questionText: How much volume of coarse aggregate in meter cube is needed if volume batching is used and the concrete mix ratio is 1:2:5 for one bag of cement?
questions.explanation: The volume of coarse aggregate can be calculated based on the mix ratio.

questions.questionText: A Foreman is supervising the concrete works in addition to masonry works, excavation, and backfill by distributing his equivalent time to those tasks on a daily basis. How much is his utilization factor in concrete work?
questions.explanation: The utilization factor is calculated based on the time distribution across tasks.

questions.questionText: A concrete work consumes a daily labor cost of birr 18,000 and daily equipment cost of birr 15,000 including all overhead costs, profits, and VAT. If the productivity for labor and equipment are 10 and 15 in cubic meters per day respectively, what will be the cost to fill 40 cubic meters of concrete?
questions.explanation: The total cost can be calculated based on the daily costs and productivity.

questions.questionText: Laboratory test is conducted according to UCSC and it is found that more than 35% of materials is smaller than sieve #200 with liquid limit greater than 50. Which of the following describes the soil type correctly?
questions.explanation: According to USCS, soil with more than 50% passing #200 sieve and LL>50 is classified as CH (high plasticity clay), not MH (high plasticity silt).

questions.questionText: A clay layer 3.66m thick rests beneath a deposit of submerged sand is 7.92m thick the top of the sand is located 3.05m below the surface of a lake. The saturated unit weight of the sand is 19.62KN/m3. The total vertical pressure and the effective vertical pressure at mid height of the clay layer respectively;
questions.explanation: The total and effective vertical pressures can be calculated based on the given parameters.

questions.questionText: Predict the degree of saturation of a 75 mm diameter and 150 mm high clay specimen with a mass of 1392.5g. When it is dried, the mass becomes 1196.5g. Assume the specific gravity of the soil grains is 2.70.
questions.explanation: The degree of saturation can be calculated using the mass and specific gravity.

questions.questionText: Assume that the soil mass is 10cm thick, 5cm high, and 14cm long that the head loss is 12cm and that k=10-3 cm/s. what is the total seepage?
questions.explanation: Total seepage can be calculated using the given parameters.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is not correct?
options: The process by which an increase in stress causes water to flow out of the soil accompanied by volume reduction is referred to as consolidation.
Soils of very low permeability (clays of high plasticity), there may be significant consolidation during construction and application of load to the foundation.
Compaction does not involve any removal of water from the soil.
Consolidation is a process that occurs in clays and silts.
questions.explanation: Option B is incorrect because in soils with very low permeability, consolidation is a slow process and significant consolidation during construction is unlikely due to the slow rate of water expulsion.

questions.questionText: A laboratory consolidation test on a normally consolidated clay showed the following results: Stress, ∆σ' (kN/m2) Void ratio at the end of consolidation, e 140 0.92 212 0.86 The specimen tested was 25.4 mm in thickness and drained on both sides. The expected maximum primary consolidation settlement in the field is: Use Sc = ∆σ' e log (H0/H1)
questions.explanation: The maximum primary consolidation settlement can be calculated using the provided data.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about stress in a soil from surface load?
options: Stress increases in radius for constant depth
Stress decreases in radius for constant depth
Stress in a soil depends on Poisson's ratio of soil
questions.explanation: Stress does not increase in radius for constant depth; it typically decreases.

questions.questionText: The most appropriate tri-axial test to assess the long-term stability of an excavated clay soil is
questions.explanation: The consolidated drained test is suitable for assessing long-term stability.

questions.questionText: Terzaghi's general bearing capacity formula for a strip footing (C Nc + q Nq + 0.5 BγNγ) gives
questions.explanation: The formula provides the ultimate bearing capacity of the footing.

questions.questionText: What is the total active thrust on a vertical wall 5m high retaining a sand of unit weight 17 kN/m3 for which the effective angle of internal friction is 35°; the surface of the sand is horizontal and the water table is below the bottom of the wall?
questions.explanation: The total active thrust can be calculated using the given parameters.

questions.questionText: During stability evaluation, the term mobilized shear strength means:
questions.explanation: Mobilized shear strength refers to the shear strength that is currently being applied.

questions.questionText: The extent of exploration does not depend on:
questions.explanation: Wind speed does not influence the extent of soil exploration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about sounding test?
options: Substantially used method to estimate the in situ undrained shear strength
The methods are based on the principle that a soil exhibiting more resistance to the penetration of a standard device is more sound
The test is conducted in a pre-bored hole
Standard penetration test is very suitable for clay soil
questions.explanation: The sounding test is based on resistance to penetration.

questions.questionText: Mat foundation is selected in the following except when:
options: When individual column footing tend to overlap
Differential setting arising out of footings.
Allowable bearing capacity of soil is high
questions.explanation: Mat foundations are not typically used when the allowable bearing capacity is high.

questions.questionText: Assume that undrained compressive strength of a soil in a site is 300kPa. It is proposed to construct a single story villa. What type of foundation has to be used?
questions.explanation: Isolated footings are suitable for low-rise structures like single-story villas.

questions.questionText: Determine the dimensions of a square footing necessary to sustain an axial column load of 850kN as shown in Fig. below, if an allowable presumptive bearing pressure of 150kN/m2 is used.
questions.explanation: The dimensions can be calculated based on the load and allowable bearing pressure.

questions.questionText: There are two phases in the design of a conventional retaining wall. From the following which one will fall under the second phase?
options: Check for the whole stability of structure
questions.explanation: Determination of steel reinforcement is part of the design phase.

questions.questionText: One of the following is incorrect about the advantage of pier foundation.
options: Bearing capacity can be increased by driving during installation.
Since no volume of soil is displaced, the problem of shifting and lifting of piles is eliminated.
Changes can be made in the design criteria during the progress of a job.
Construction equipment is normally mobile and construction can proceed rapidly.
questions.explanation: The statement about increasing bearing capacity by driving is not entirely accurate.

questions.questionText: The allowable working load on a pre-stressed concrete pile 21 m long that has been driven into sand is 502 kN. The pile is octagonal in shape with D = 356 mm. Skin resistance carries 350 kN of the allowable load, and point bearing carries the rest. Use Ep = 21 x 10^6 kN/m2, Es = 25 x 10^3 kN/m2, μs = 0.35, and ξ = 0.62. Evaluate elastic shortening of the pile.
questions.explanation: Elastic shortening can be calculated based on the given parameters.

questions.questionText: One of the following is NOT categorized as best cell fill property for the construction of cellular coffer dam.
options: Is free-draining (large coefficient of permeability, k)
Has a high angle of internal friction, ϕ
Contains small amounts of No. 200 sieve material — preferably less than 5 percent
Contains large amounts of No. 200 sieve material — preferably greater than 5 percent
questions.explanation: Large amounts of No. 200 sieve material are not preferred for cellular coffer dams.

questions.questionText: _____________ controls design of foundation on expansive soils.
questions.explanation: Heave is a critical factor in designing foundations on expansive soils.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a remediation method for contaminated sites due to problems in geotechnical engineering.
options: Replacement of contaminated soil and waste
questions.explanation: Stabilizing soil materials is not typically a remediation method for contamination.

questions.questionText: Civil engineering infrastructure development projects impacted greatly on the environment except:
options: Increase in size of available land
questions.explanation: Infrastructure projects typically do not increase the size of available land.

questions.questionText: Which of the following type of dam is built in areas where the foundation is not strong enough to bear the weight of concrete?
questions.explanation: Earth dams are suitable for weak foundations due to their lighter weight.

questions.questionText: A homogeneous earth fill dam has the distance from the focus to the directrix of seepage line (yo) = 14.5m and Coefficient permeability of 1.5 x 10^-5 m/sec. Determine the seepage passing through per unit length of the dam?
questions.explanation: Seepage can be calculated using the given parameters.

questions.questionText: What is the discharge passing over a high ogee spillway with effective length of 30m and design head of 2.5m?
questions.explanation: Discharge can be calculated using the spillway design parameters.

questions.questionText: Which of the following criteria has to be satisfied for no tension at any point on a gravity dam?
options: The resultant of all the forces must always pass through the mid-point of the base of the dam
The resultant force for all conditions of loading must pass through the middle third of the base
The resultant of all the forces must pass through the upstream extremity of the middle third of the base
The resultant of all the forces must pass through the downstream extremity of the middle third of the base
questions.explanation: The resultant force must pass through the middle third of the base to avoid tension.

questions.questionText: Which one is the correct sequence from the reservoir in the direction of the flow of water for the installation of a hydropower plant?
options: Reservoir, Head Race Tunnel, surge tank, turbine, penstock
Reservoir, Head Race Tunnel, surge tank, penstock, turbine
Reservoir, Head Race Tunnel, penstock, surge tank, turbine
Reservoir, Head Race Tunnel, surge tank, turbine, penstock
questions.explanation: The correct sequence for water flow in a hydropower plant is provided.

questions.questionText: Which of the following application Software is used to analyze and solve the factor of safety of embankment dams for slope stability and locate phreatic line through the body of the dam?
questions.explanation: GeoSLOPE is used for slope stability analysis in embankment dams.

questions.questionText: A reservoir of glycerin has a mass of 1200Kg and a volume of 0.952m3. The glycerin weight (W); mass density (ρ); Specific weight (γ); and Specific gravity (Sg) respectively are______
questions.explanation: The values can be calculated based on the mass and volume of glycerin.
